sections.heading: Notice of Update Distribution
sections.markdown:
We are distributing an update to improve the stability of gameplay and to adjust balance.

We apologize for the inconvenience, but please apply the latest update before you enjoy the game.

Targeted platforms:

- PlayStation 4
- PlayStation 5
- Xbox One
- Xbox Series X|S
- Steam

The version number of this update shown at the lower right corner of the Title Screen will be as follows:

- App Ver. 1.03
- Regulation Ver. 1.03.1

sections.heading: Changes
sections.markdown: Major Changes Included in the Latest Update

sections.heading: Additional Elements Added
sections.markdown:
- Added a function to record an icon and the name of an NPC on the map when you encounter that NPC.
- Added NPC Jar-Bairn.
- Added new quest phases for the following NPCs: Diallos / Nepheli Loux / Kenneth Haight / Gatekeeper Gostoc.
- Added some summonable NPCs in multiple situations
- Increased the number of patterns of objects player can imitate when using Mimic’s Veil.
- Added night background music for some open field area.

- Increased the drop rate of Smithing Stone for some enemies.

- Increased shield’s effectiveness.
- Increased the damage for all offensive cracked pot items.

- Increased the effect duration for the following items: Uplifting Aromatic / Ironjar Aromatic.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Flame of the Fell God** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Giants' Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Guaranteed Drop**: Liurnia of the Lakes
- Received upon defeating Adan, Thief of Fire, the boss trapped in the Malefactor's Evergaol.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Summons a raging fireball that deals Fire Attack Power equal to 415% of Incantation Scaling and explodes upon impact with a 3.5 meter radius, leaving lingering fire spots for 7 seconds that appear to be able to hit about once per second with Fire Attack Power equal to 35% of Incantation Scaling and a 1 meter effect radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 34 FP per cast.
- Costs 42 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 2 Memory Slots to equip.
- The projectile is quite large but travels slowly.
- Upon detonation, the spell applies a knockback effect to targets.
- The explosion deals 16 Stance damage, while each tick from the fire spots deals 1 Stance damage.
- Only one Flame of the Fell God can be active per player at a time. Casting a new one will remove the previous fireball, but lingering hazard spots will persist even after a new flame is cast.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- This spell is highly effective against Erdtree Avatars, as they are weak to Fire and rarely reposition during combat.
- The damage of the lingering fire spots is usually reduced to insignificance by an enemy's flat defense. However, their consistent Stance damage can prevent an enemy's Stance from regenerating for up to 7 seconds.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Update 1.07:
 - The FP cost was reduced from 42 to 34.
 - Increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
 - The stamina attack power of the explosion was increased from 190 to 360 (450 against players).
 - The stamina attack power of the residual flame hazard was increased from 20 to 40 (50 against players). Additionally, their hit frequency was increased to approximately once per second.
- Update 1.04:
 - The FP cost was reduced from 50 to 42.
 - The explosion damage of the fireball was increased from 352% to 415% of Incantation Scaling.

- The fell god was said to have been defeated by Queen Marika the Eternal before the Age of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Flame, Cleanse Me** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Fire Monk incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Loot**: Liurnia of the Lakes
- Flame, Cleanse Me can be looted from a corpse at the Fire Monk campsite located south of the Church of Vows in eastern Liurnia.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Alleviates buildup of the Poison and Scarlet Rot status effects and cures Frostbite, Poison, and Scarlet Rot.

Deals 15 HP damage to the caster.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 14 FP per cast.
- Costs 10 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- The reason that Frostbite is only removed when fully applied instead of also when it's building up is because the flat HP damage is considered to be Fire damage, and an effect of that damage type is that it removes applied Frostbite.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- This incantation is considered vital for navigating swamp areas filled with Poison and Scarlet Rot.
 - This is especially true for Scarlet Rot areas as other means of removing it is either in limited supply (Preserving Boluses) or only get one use without resting at a Site of Grace again (Speckled Hardtear).
 - While technically only the Prophet and Confessor origins have enough Faith to use this incantation by default, it can still be used by any starting Origin's at base Faith by using the Two Fingers Heirloom (a Prisoner will need another point in Faith, easiest gained with either Marika's Scarseal or a Commoner's Garb or Commoner's Simple Garb).
 - All Origins also start with enough FP to cast this incantation at least 3 times without using a Flask of Cerulean Tears, provided they haven't used any FP for anything too expensive.

sections.markdown: Flame, Fall Upon Them** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Giants' Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 10,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Giant's Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
 - WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Flings 12 balls of fire each with Fire Attack Power equal to 115% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 140% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 16 FP per cast.
- Costs 40 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 52 points.
 - Technically the Stamina cost is 10 points for the uncharged version and 13 for the charged version, but the cost is taken 4 times.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 4 Stance damage per hit (12 at most). Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 6 (18 at most).
- The initial fireball will split into 12 after traveling a short distance.
- At most 3 of the small fireballs can damage a single target. This limits the effective maximum Attack Power of this spell towards a singlet target to roughtly 345% of Incantation Scaling, or 420% of the same when charged.
- When charged, the fireballs will explode on impact to deal area-of-effect (AoE) damage.
- Inflicts additional Stamina damage to blocking targets.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.markdown:
- Godfrey Icon increases the Attack Power of charged attacks by 15%.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 22%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of ??%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Each fireball deals individual damage, and hitting with multiple fireballs can greatly increase damage output.
- This spell is highly effective against large targets, as most or all fireballs can hit, and works well for groups due to its solid AoE damage, low FP cost, and quick casting.
- At close range, only the initial fireball may hit before splitting, so midrange is ideal for landing multiple hits.
- The wide spread and AoE of the fireballs can catch evasive enemies, making it useful against invaders or invisible Teardrop Scarabs.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Flame, Protect Me** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Fire Monk incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot**: Mountaintops of the Giants
- Flame, Protect Me can be found in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave in the Mountaintops of the Giants. It is located behind an imp statue fog wall right next to the dungeon's grace. One Stonesword Key is required to access it.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Flame, Protect Me applies a Body Buff that increases Fire Damage Negation by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 30 FP per cast.
- Costs 20 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.

- This incantation reduces damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total Fire damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *FlameProtect* represents the PvE/PvP effect multiplier:
- : TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {FireDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {FlameProtect}) ) 
 - For example, if Fire damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 70%:
 - : TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.60) ) = 70% 
 - Against other players, the total reduction would be 40%:
 - : TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.20) ) = 40%

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.markdown: - Old Lord's Talisman extends the duration from 70 to 91 seconds.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Acquired very late, most often after every significant Fire-heavy area and boss except for Mountaintops of the Giants itself and the Fire Giant, and perhaps Dragonlord Placidusax.
 - If doing the Volcano Manor questline to access Praetor Rykard, then he can be fought after acquiring this incantation since the last assassination also takes place in Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave
- This is the only improved elemental defense buff that doesn't also apply to nearby allies.
 - The only way to also buff nearby allies with Fire Damage Negation is Protection of the Erdtree, which also increases Holy, Lightning, and Magic Damage Negation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - This incantation is one of the oldest known techniques among the Fire Monks.

sections.markdown:
Calls on two red, crackling spears from above that is then slammed into the ground, hitting with Lightning Attack Power equal to 367% of Incantation Scaling in a small 0.2 meter radius, and creating a shockwave with a 3 meter radius that hits with Lightning Attack Power equal to 288% of Incantation Scaling.

From the point of impact, waves of red lightning are sent out directly ahead and behind, and to the left and right of the caster with Lightning Attack Power equal to 122% of Incantation Scaling in a 2 meter radius from the center of each wave.

The second spear is slammed down as the first spear's waves are spreading, repeating the process but with the power of the direct hit increasing to 374% of Incantation Scaling, the shockwave hit to 292% of the same, and the wave hit to 123% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Casting the spell costs 42 points of Stamina.
- Deals 16.8 Stance damage on a direct or shockwave hit and 5 Stance damage on a wave hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- The "direct" hit and the initial area attack cannot hit the same target, though the smaller, weakest waves can hit an enemy that has already been hit if they are either quick or large enough to also be where those are.
- The "spears" are actually flung downwards, meaning they can be used to hit the ground beneath a cliff if the caster is standing on its edge.
- Has a much longer casting time than Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear due to having two spears, but each hit is stronger.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
 - FP cost was reduced from 45 to 35.
 - Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 100 to 140 on the direct hit with the first spear and from 120 to 160 with the second spear.
 - Separate Stamina Attack Power values for guarding players: for the first spear the direct hit was increased from 140 to 175, the shockwave hit was increased from 100 to 125, and the wave hit was increased from 60 to 75, while for the second spear the direct hit was increased from 160 to 200, the shockwave hit was increased from 120 to 150, and the wave hit was increased from 60 to 75.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost, increased cast speed and decreased recovery time, and allows caster to withstand enemy attack while casting more easily.
 - FP cost was reduced from 65 to 45.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of blue flames, dealing Magic damage equal to 159% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e. 477% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast, and another 40 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Smarag's Glintstone Breath.
- Compared to Smarag's Glintstone Breath, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 30% less FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 104 FP: 2*28 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
 - Only 53 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the strongest "default" dragon breath attack, though as it only does 10% more damage than Dragonfire, if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation is lower than its Magic Damage Negation that will change.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.markdown: The **Formless Mother** (姿なき母, *Sugata-naki Haha*), also known as **Mother of Truth** (真実の母, *Shinjitsu no Haha*), is an Outer God in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Formless Mother was encountered by Mohg deep underground. She is known to crave wounds, and to bestow power upon accursed blood. Her body can be pierced using Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear, causing the weapon to become coated in Bloodflame, or an arm can be thrust into her body in order to scatter Bloodflame on the ground, using the incantation Bloodboon.

The mother of truth offered the residents of Prospect Town salvation and transformed them into bloodfiends.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Formless Mother is omnipresent and can be stabbed from anywhere in the Lands Between by using a ritual spear.
- Although never directly stated, many details point to the Land of Reeds being under the influence of the Formless Mother. Descriptions of Reedlanders as having "succumbed to a blood-soaked madness" and their clear favoritism for weapons that cause Blood Loss all point towards the work of the Outer God. The magical enhancement granded by the forbidden Reedlander combat technique, Seppuku, may very well be a blessing from the Formless Mother, with the technique acting as a form of offering. Additionally, both Okina and Eleonora join Mohg's Bloody Fingers.
- The entity responsible for the Thorn Sorceries, Briars of Punishment and Briars of Sin, referred to as the blood star, the may have some connection to the Formless Mother. It is entirely possible due to their perceived values of spilling blood and inflicting wounds, that the Formless Mother and "the blood star", could be one in the same.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - The Mother's designation as "Formless" resembles the title of a Great One (conceptually similar to an Outer God) that is indirectly featured in the FromSoftware game *Bloodborne*, called "Formless Oedon" (姿なきオドン, *Sugata-naki Odon*). In fact, both entities are strongly associated with blood.

sections.markdown: Giant Land Octopuses** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Giant Land Octopuses are bloodless creatures commonly found near bodies of water throughout the Lands Between. Their elastic bodies resemble writhing masses of tentacles, with two primary limbs used for combat. A beak protrudes from their central mass, nestled between these appendages. These creatures consume humans to nourish their otherwise pale ovaries. Their Land Octopus offspring are enlivened by a lingering warmth reminiscent of human skin.

Despite their sluggish nature, they react aggressively when approached, striking with unpredictable, sweeping attacks. Their primary method of attack involves flailing their tentacles in a wild barrage, making them dangerous at close range. Attacking their beak can stagger them, creating an opening for a critical strike.

These creatures are capable of regenerating tentacles, which can be severed with well-aimed attacks. They may consume their tentacles mid-combat to restore a portion of their health.

These creatures exhibit high durability and resist most forms of damage, except for direct attacks to their beak. However, they are especially vulnerable to Frostbite, making weapons that inflict it particularly effective.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Takes reduced damage everywhere except the beak.
- If staggered, a critical attack can be performed on its beak.
- Tentacles can be severed, reducing its attack range. However, it can regenerate them by consuming one of its remaining limbs.
- Can be interrupted while healing if staggered before the animation completes.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Background

Ghostflame was an ancient death hex produced by burning the bones of the dead. It was kept in kilns by Deathbirds—progeny of the Twinbird—who used it to unbind and release vengeful spirits, raked from the ashes with Death's Poker. Ancient death hexes like Rancorcall and Ancient Death Rancor were created or discovered and used as sorceries by the servants of Death long ago.

The Company of the Fallen Hawk was sent deep underground to explore the buried ruins of the Eternal Cities, but when their resources were exhausted, they burned the bodies of their companions for light. They acquired the cold ghostflame, but condemned themselves to inhabit the underground for eternity.

sections.markdown: , also known as **First-Generation Albinaurics**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The bearded Elder Albinaurics were gaunt, lanky men born from a drop of silver dew, artificially created by human hands. The immovable first generation Albinaurics had dysfunctional shins and could only crawl, their legs fading as death approached. When their legs vanished completely, so too did their lives. To compensate for their immobility, many became glintstone sorcerers, casting spells using blue glintstone and their innate arcane power, while others took to acting through puppets.

Due to the circumstances surrounding their occult origin, they were deemed impure and shunned by many inhabitants of the Lands Between. The Albinaurics were spurned from the Erdtree's grace, and suffered heavy persecution at the hands of the brutal Cuckoo Knights of Raya Lucaria. After the Shattering, the agents of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing attacked the Village of the Albinaurics and massacred its residents in search of the Haligree Secret Medallion. And so, the Albinaurics of old pleaded to the stars, night, and fate for to punish the world that condemned them.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: An Albinauric villager living in the Village of the Albinaurics. They move by dragging themselves with their hands and attack by lunging at foes or shoving them back. Sometimes, they will feign death before ambushing their foes in groups.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: An Albinauric sorcerer that uses their arcane nature and an Albinauric Staff to cast Glintstone Pebble. Albinauric sorcerers in Caria Manor and Volcano Manor can cast Magic Downpour.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: A sickly Albinauric consumed by poison. They can be found in the swamp surrounding the Village of the Albinaurics, periodically coughing up poisonous mist.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: An Albinauric prisoner locked in a pillory, at times suspended from the ceilings of Volcano Manor and Castle Sol to act the part of sentries. When an intruder approaches, they will scream to alert nearby allies. In Castle Sol, the screams of these sentries are capable of manifesting the spirits of Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: An Albinauric prisoner forced to wear a Black Dumpling. Driven to insanity, they will lunge and tear at their foe. They have a unique grab attack where they hold down the foe and rip their throat with their teeth.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Old Albus is a friendly Elder Albinauric character at the Village of the Albinaurics. He is initially disguised as a pot.
- Pidia, Carian Servant is an Elder Albinauric Sorcerer at Caria Manor. He acts as a merchant and maintains the puppets.
- First-Generation Albinauric are the male counterparts to Albinauric Archers, who appear younger and ride Wolves.
- First-Generation Albinaurics seek Miquella's Haligtree and Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

- The also known as the shinbone or shankbone, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee. The first generation of Albinaurics lost the use of their tibias, and are unable to walk on their own.
- Elder Albinaurics wear Headbands of the Golden Ones.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Frostbite** is a status effect in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.markdown: Frostbite accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Robustness stat, the longer it will take for Frostbite to become effective. Robustness can be increased by increasing the Endurance stat. Once effective, the player will take a flat amount of damage, and take increased damage from other sources until the effect wears off.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Frenzyflame Stone** is craftable item in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Throws a stone on the ground that heals specific subjects within vicinity of the source.
- Heals 35 HP per second.
- Lasts 30 seconds before wearing off.
- Can only heal any of these creatures / enemies:
 - Player who has inherited the Frenzied Flame (If the player has used Miquella's Needle then they'll be unable to benefit from this item until they can inherit it again in a second playthrough)
 - Frenzied Rat
 - Frenzied Commoner
 - Frenzied Flame Foot Soldier
 - Frenzied Flame Soldier
 - Frenzied Flame Knight
 - Frenzied Troll
 - Nomad
 - Nomad Ashes
- Any humans in the radius who has not inherited the Frenzied Flame (including human NPCs) gain a buildup of 15 points of Madness per second while in the stone's radius.
 - Does not cause madness towards friendly NPCs.
- Healing effects stack with Warming Stones for a total of 60 HP regeneration per second.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A cave beneath Fort Gael which has been converted into a prison, accessible by crossing a pool of Scarlet Rot and unlocked using a Stonesword Key. The intricate cave system features many locked cells, containing enemies and loot. In the depths of the cave is a chamber occupied by vulgar militiamen, as well as a lever which will unlock the cells when pulled.
The boss room opens onto a cliff in Limgrave.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Fire Prelates** are Enemies in Elden Ring and Bosses in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Fire Prelates were commanders of the Fire Monks who once aided the champions of the Erdtree during the War Against the Giants and later became guardians of the Flame of Ruin. Their weighty frames symbolized the onus of the vows they took as guardians of the Flame. Their helmets were topped with cauldrons that once contained embers that would surge into flame when their faith reached its zenith. The most hallowed Prelate, Birac, once severed his own head to teach humility to his kin. His head was later made into the Cranial Vessel Candlestand.

Most wielded heavy hammers, croziers symbolizing their guardianship, while others carry whips fashioned in the image of the Briars of Sin.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown: - Fire Prelates spawn in the Crater in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Wears Fire Prelate Helm, Fire Prelate Gauntlets, Fire Prelate Greaves, and either Fire Prelate Armor or Fire Prelate Armor (Altered)
- Wields Prelate's Inferno Crozier or Thorned Whip
- The helm depicts Birac with an awakened third eye on his forehead.
- The chest emblem depicts two hands grasping the stem of a sunflower engulfed in flame. It resembles the burning Staff of the Guilty held by Guilty.
- Some Golem Smiths also bear similar bowl-like heads.
- The striking face of their hammer resembles a blazing red sun or a Torrent of Life.
- They have red hair.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Flame Chariots** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A Flame Chariot is a highly-mobile, armored war machine cast in bronze and modeled on the face of a Fire Giant, its braided beard reimagined as sharpened metal tusks. Constructed and operated by Fire Monks, it ignites oil stored in its head to produce makeshift Giants' Flame incantations, expelled from molten, tongue-like cannons. Designed to charge through enemy ranks, this tank then spins rapidly while scorching the area in steady streams of fire. A protective layer of verdigris coats its chassis, and its front bumpers proudly displays the crest of a golden hawk. Its eyes carefully track its targets, and a spiked corona adorns its scalp.

Flame Chariots are manned by teams of three Foot Soldiers, including one pilot, who sits in a cabin at the rear of the vehicle, and two unseen wheel operators. They are near-impenetrable, but can be destroyed instantly by killing the driver, whose backside is exposed, or with a plunging Critical Attack by dropping down onto their chimneys from above, rigging them to explode.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Stance: 240
- Deals Strike and Fire damage.
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to a Critical Attack after a Stance break
- Vulnerable to backstabbing Critical Attacks
- Five-Tongued Fire Chariots produce five streams of flame on all attacks.
- According to concept art, there are two additional operators inside the Flame Chariot.
- Flame Chariots appear in Elden Ring Nightreign.
 - Three Flame Chariots are the Boss of Fire-affinity Main Encampments.
 - Enemy variants patrol a ruined roadway deep within the Crater.
- Marika's Rune forms at the center of its wrinkled brow.
- A ring of eight bolts encircle the cap to each wooden wheel.

sections.markdown: The **First Church of Marika** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A church in northeastern Mountaintops of the Giants, southeast of the Freezing Lake. This is the site of Queen Marika's address to Godfrey and his men, when she commanded him to put the Fire Giants to the sword in the War Against the Giants, ushering the start of her age of the Erdtree.

It contains a statue of Queen Marika the Eternal and is surrounded by the spirits of coniferous trees.
